expressibility_gap.why: kw9.5 ledger 0002: the check surface has no cardinality claim over stored arrows; declaring the collision would be a derived relation (the P3 boundary). The bench measures whether ANY arm detects it — the gap is the object under test, restated here because it licenses the B expectation; kw9.11 confirms it empirically for both categorical arms (B and C silent on all three collisions)

discrepancies: D1 (arms.md S1 seeding wording vs its own registered result): arms.md says 'Append one capture row', but the registered result in both protocol files is a 4th collision with '2 stored capture rows, one shared sha256' (README review note 7: 'a duplicated pair'); one appended row yields a 1-match selector and cannot satisfy the pinned A-must-report-4 expectation. kw9.11 implemented the pair (two copies of the slice's first capture under bench-seed/s1, ids bfc:bench-seed-s1 / bfc:bench-seed-s1-2, revisions bench-seed-s1 / bench-seed-s1-2), applied identically to arms A, B and C. Recorded, not silent.

D2 (dangling faults fire at load, not on the check surface): S2 (arms B and C) and the recipe's overconstraint control are caught by the .ct.json v1 loader as labeled errors (exit 1, `error[syntax]` naming the dangling table cell) rather than as check-surface violations (exit 3). The registrations require a non-zero exit / that the battery catches the fault — satisfied verbatim; the exit-3 wording in the recipe/README is not reachable for dangling stored references on this loader. The firings are recorded verbatim and scored as sanity outcomes, never as check detections (rubric: only check violations are detections).

D3 (arm-C search bounds): the natural-bounds search (--rows naming the declared objects' real row counts) returned UNKNOWN within the 256-candidate default; per the recipe an UNKNOWN payload means shrink the bounds, never declare success — bounds were shrunk (all seven objects at 1), and the recorded outcome is `witness within bounds`, a bounded-run success, not a clean bill (rubric non-finding).

D4 (drafter disclosure, honesty rule): the arm-C drafting agent is this session's model (GLM, Z.ai — the kw9.11 worker agent), not an independent session. The drafter had earlier in the same session read slice.json while building arm A and the seeding harness, so the draft step was not prose-blind in the strict sense; the draft's schema was written from the prose block only, and its instance rows were taken verbatim from instance-slice.json (the prose's designated input), which the recorded instance-custody diff confirms byte-for-byte derivable from the frozen slice rows.

D5 (pre-registration commit hash): the arms.md ledger template pins `commit <hash>` of the kw9.6 pre-registration; the ticket forbids git commands in kw9.11, so the hash is left un-recorded here and the protocol is cited by path (fixtures/probes/bench/README.md + arms.md).

D6 (arm-A selector-set provenance): slice.json carries no selector table, so arm A's selector set is DISTINCT (source, edition_date) over the slice's capture and partition rows (3 selectors — exactly the collision selectors); the 127 zero-match negatives of E4 are scored via the floor run (census criterion over all 127: zero detections), matching census.json's frozen denominators.
